title: OCR inspect masks unexpected resolver failures as normal resolution errors
reasoning: The route catches every Exception raised while resolving OCR coordinates and serializes it into the successful OcrInspectResponse as resolution_error. That is appropriate for expected OCR resolution failures, but it also hides unexpected programmer/runtime errors from OcrCoordinateResolver.resolve or the surrounding mapping logic as a 200 response. Clients cannot distinguish a genuine no-match condition from a backend failure, and monitoring/error handling will miss the failure path.
recommendation: Catch only the expected OCR resolution exception types, or have build_ocr_resolution_error indicate whether the exception is known and re-raise/log unknown exceptions as server errors.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for POST /api/sdk/ocr/inspect, and the route currently has no visible regression assertion for unexpected resolver exceptions versus expected resolution misses.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused route/service test that makes OcrCoordinateResolver.resolve raise an unexpected RuntimeError and asserts the request fails with a server error instead of returning a successful response with resolution_error.
minimumFixScope: Limit the change to sdk_ocr_inspect exception handling and the expected OCR resolution error type boundary.
